atoms.text: This guide configures the FrameForge transcoding service to read mezzanine video files from the bucket studio-masters and write MP4 renditions back to the same bucket. The service runs under the IAM role frameforge-transcode-role in account 111122223333, which also owns the bucket. Because the role and the bucket are in the same account, access is granted entirely by the role's identity-based policy. Attach a policy to the role that allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::studio-masters/masters/* and s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::studio-masters/renditions/*. Add s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::studio-masters with an s3:prefix condition of masters/ so the service can enumerate pending jobs. Leave the bucket policy unchanged, since no statement is required there for this role. Verify the setup by submitting a test job that reads masters/test-clip.mov and confirming that renditions/test-clip_1080p.mp4 is created. If the job fails with AccessDenied, check the role policy for resource ARN typos and for explicit Deny statements.

This guide configures the FrameForge transcoding service to read mezzanine video files from the bucket studio-masters and write MP4 renditions back to the same bucket. The service runs under the IAM role frameforge-transcode-role in account 444455556666, while the bucket is owned by account 111122223333. Because the role and the bucket are in different accounts, the bucket owner grants access by adding a statement to the bucket policy. In that statement, set the Principal to arn:aws:iam::444455556666:role/frameforge-transcode-role and allow s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::studio-masters/masters/* and s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::studio-masters/renditions/*. Add s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::studio-masters with an s3:prefix condition of masters/ so the service can enumerate pending jobs. The bucket owner applies this change in account 111122223333. Verify the setup by submitting a test job that reads masters/test-clip.mov and confirming that renditions/test-clip_1080p.mp4 is created. If the job fails with AccessDenied, check the bucket policy for a mistyped principal ARN and for explicit Deny statements.

This guide allows the ScanLoom OCR service to read scanned PDF files from the bucket intake-scans and write extracted text as JSON to the same bucket. The service uses the IAM role scanloom-ocr-role in account 222233334444, which also owns the bucket. Since both are in one account, the grant is made in the role's identity-based policy alone. Attach a policy that allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::intake-scans/incoming/* and s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::intake-scans/text/*. Also allow s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::intake-scans with an s3:prefix condition of incoming/ so the service can detect new files. No change is made to the bucket policy. To test, upload incoming/invoice-0001.pdf and wait for the service to write text/invoice-0001.json. If the output does not appear, review the role's policy for a missing PutObject action or a mismatched prefix.

This guide allows the ScanLoom OCR service to read scanned PDF files from the bucket intake-scans and write extracted text as JSON to the same bucket. The service uses the IAM role scanloom-ocr-role in account 555566667777, and the bucket is owned by account 222233334444. Since the two are in different accounts, the bucket owner makes the grant in the bucket policy. Add a statement with the Principal arn:aws:iam::555566667777:role/scanloom-ocr-role that allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::intake-scans/incoming/* and s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::intake-scans/text/*. Also allow s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::intake-scans with an s3:prefix condition of incoming/ so the service can detect new files. The bucket owner saves this updated policy on the bucket in account 222233334444. To test, upload incoming/invoice-0001.pdf and wait for the service to write text/invoice-0001.json. If the output does not appear, review the bucket policy for a missing PutObject action or a mismatched prefix.

This guide sets up the PixelTrim image service to read original photographs from the bucket catalog-images and write resized thumbnails under a separate prefix. PixelTrim runs as the IAM role pixeltrim-worker in account 333344445555, the same account that owns the bucket. The grant is therefore carried by the role's identity-based policy, and the bucket policy stays as it is. Attach a policy that allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::catalog-images/originals/*. In the same policy, allow s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::catalog-images/thumbnails/* and nothing else for writes. The service generates 128, 256, and 512 pixel variants, so all three output paths fall under the thumbnails prefix. Test by placing originals/sku-8841.jpg in the bucket and checking for thumbnails/sku-8841_256.jpg. A 403 response usually indicates that the policy is not attached to the role or that the resource ARN does not match the prefix.

This guide sets up the PixelTrim image service to read original photographs from the bucket catalog-images and write resized thumbnails under a separate prefix. PixelTrim runs as the IAM role pixeltrim-worker in account 666677778888, and the bucket belongs to account 333344445555. The grant is therefore carried by a statement in the bucket policy that the bucket owner adds. Set the statement's Principal to arn:aws:iam::666677778888:role/pixeltrim-worker and allow s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::catalog-images/originals/*. In the same statement or a second one, allow s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::catalog-images/thumbnails/* and nothing else for writes. The service generates 128, 256, and 512 pixel variants, so all three output paths fall under the thumbnails prefix. Test by placing originals/sku-8841.jpg in the bucket and checking for thumbnails/sku-8841_256.jpg. A 403 response usually indicates that the principal ARN in the bucket policy is wrong or that the resource ARN does not match the prefix.

This guide gives the VoxIndex transcription service access to audio recordings in the bucket call-recordings and permission to store transcript files there. The service assumes the IAM role voxindex-service-role in account 444455556677, which is also the bucket owner. Same-account access is granted through the role's identity-based policy, so the bucket policy is not modified. The policy should allow s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::call-recordings/audio/*, which holds WAV and FLAC files. It should also allow s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::call-recordings/transcripts/* for the WebVTT and JSON output. Add s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN restricted to the audio/ prefix. After attaching the policy, upload audio/call-20240301-a.wav and wait for transcripts/call-20240301-a.json to be written. If the transcript is missing, check the service logs for AccessDenied errors and compare the denied resource to the policy.

This guide gives the VoxIndex transcription service access to audio recordings in the bucket call-recordings and permission to store transcript files there. The service assumes the IAM role voxindex-service-role in account 777788889999, while account 444455556677 owns the bucket. Cross-account access is granted by the bucket owner through a bucket policy statement. The statement names the principal arn:aws:iam::777788889999:role/voxindex-service-role and allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::call-recordings/audio/*, which holds WAV and FLAC files. It also allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::call-recordings/transcripts/* for the WebVTT and JSON output. Add s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN restricted to the audio/ prefix. After the owner saves the policy, upload audio/call-20240301-a.wav and wait for transcripts/call-20240301-a.json to be written. If the transcript is missing, check the service logs for AccessDenied errors and compare the denied resource to the bucket policy.

This guide configures the PageMill document conversion service to read DOCX files from the bucket legal-drafts and write PDF output to the same bucket. PageMill runs under the IAM role pagemill-convert-role in account 555566667788, and that account owns the bucket. Access is granted by the role's identity-based policy; the bucket policy is not edited. Allow s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::legal-drafts/docx/* and s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::legal-drafts/pdf/*. Include s3:AbortMultipartUpload on the pdf/ prefix because large conversions are uploaded in parts. Files that fail conversion are not written, so no error prefix permission is needed. Test by uploading docx/contract-17.docx and confirming that pdf/contract-17.pdf is created with a nonzero size. If the upload stalls, verify that the multipart actions are present in the policy attached to the role.

PageMill runs under the IAM role pagemill-convert-role in account 888899990000, and the bucket is owned by account 555566667788. The bucket owner grants access by adding a statement to the bucket policy. Set the Principal to arn:aws:iam::888899990000:role/pagemill-convert-role and allow s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::legal-drafts/docx/* and s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::legal-drafts/pdf/*. Include s3:AbortMultipartUpload on the pdf/ prefix because large conversions are uploaded in parts. Files that fail conversion are not written, so no error prefix permission is needed. Test by uploading docx/contract-17.docx and confirming that pdf/contract-17.pdf is created with a nonzero size. If the upload stalls, verify that the multipart actions are present in the bucket policy statement.

This guide enables the CaptionWright service to read video files and SRT subtitle files from the bucket broadcast-staging and write captioned video back to it. The service uses the IAM role captionwright-burnin-role in account 666677778899, which owns the bucket. Because the role and bucket share an account, the role's identity-based policy carries the permissions. Allow s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::broadcast-staging/video/* and arn:aws:s3:::broadcast-staging/subtitles/*. Allow s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::broadcast-staging/captioned/* so the burned-in output has its own location. The bucket policy remains unchanged, including its existing statements for other users. Test by placing video/ep12.mp4 and subtitles/ep12.srt in the bucket and waiting for captioned/ep12.mp4. If the output is absent, confirm that the policy covers both input prefixes, since a missing subtitles path causes the job to fail.

This guide enables the CaptionWright service to read video files and SRT subtitle files from the bucket broadcast-staging and write captioned video back to it. The service uses the IAM role captionwright-burnin-role in account 999900001111, and the bucket belongs to account 666677778899. Because the role is external to the bucket's account, the bucket owner adds the grant to the bucket policy. Name arn:aws:iam::999900001111:role/captionwright-burnin-role as the Principal and allow s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::broadcast-staging/video/* and arn:aws:s3:::broadcast-staging/subtitles/*. Allow s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::broadcast-staging/captioned/* so the burned-in output has its own location. The new statement is added alongside the bucket's existing statements for other users. Test by placing video/ep12.mp4 and subtitles/ep12.srt in the bucket and waiting for captioned/ep12.mp4. If the output is absent, confirm that the statement covers both input prefixes, since a missing subtitles path causes the job to fail.

This guide grants the MarkStamp watermarking service access to a bucket of stock photos, reading unmarked images and writing watermarked copies. The service runs as the IAM role markstamp-batch-role in account 777788889900, and that account owns the bucket stock-gallery. Permissions are set in the role's identity-based policy, and the bucket policy is left untouched. Allow s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::stock-gallery/clean/* and s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::stock-gallery/marked/*. Do not allow s3:DeleteObject, because the service must never remove source images. Batch runs list the clean/ prefix, so add s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::stock-gallery with an s3:prefix condition of clean/. Verify with a batch of ten images from clean/set-04/ and check that ten matching objects appear under marked/set-04/. A missing object usually means the list permission or the output path in the policy is wrong.

This guide grants the MarkStamp watermarking service access to a bucket of stock photos, reading unmarked images and writing watermarked copies. The service runs as the IAM role markstamp-batch-role in account 000011112222, and account 777788889900 owns the bucket stock-gallery. The bucket owner sets the permissions in a bucket policy statement that names the role's account. Use the Principal arn:aws:iam::000011112222:root and allow s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::stock-gallery/clean/* and s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::stock-gallery/marked/*. Do not allow s3:DeleteObject, because the service must never remove source images. Batch runs list the clean/ prefix, so add s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::stock-gallery with an s3:prefix condition of clean/. Verify with a batch of ten images from clean/set-04/ and check that ten matching objects appear under marked/set-04/. A missing object usually means the list permission or the output path in the bucket policy is wrong.

This guide lets the MetaHarvest service read e-book files from the bucket publishing-archive and write extracted metadata as sidecar JSON files. MetaHarvest runs under the IAM role metaharvest-extract-role in account 888899990011, the account that owns the bucket. The role's identity-based policy grants all required access, and the bucket policy is not changed. Allow s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::publishing-archive/epub/* and s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::publishing-archive/metadata/*. Each EPUB produces one JSON file named after the source, such as metadata/title-204.json for epub/title-204.epub. Add s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN with an s3:prefix condition of epub/ so the service can page through the archive. Test by running the service against a single file and checking that the JSON contains the title, author, and language fields. If the service reports AccessDenied on write, confirm that the output path in the policy is metadata/ and not epub/.

Set the Principal to arn:aws:iam::111122223399:role/metaharvest-extract-role, allow s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::publishing-archive/epub/*, and allow s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::publishing-archive/metadata/*. Each EPUB produces one JSON file named after the source, such as metadata/title-204.json for epub/title-204.epub. Test by running the service against a single file and checking that the JSON contains the title, author, and language fields. If the service reports AccessDenied on write, confirm that the output path in the bucket policy is metadata/ and not epub/.
